actions.name: acquire-worktree
actions.doc: An isolated checkout for one piece of work, created or reused.

actions.name: discuss
actions.doc: Answer a person's turn in a discussion, before anything is decided.

actions.name: draft-plan
actions.doc: Ask the agent for a piece of writing, in whoever asked's own words.

actions.name: hand-over
actions.doc: A write handed to the operator instead of made: said once, in the work's thread when there is one and the notifier otherwise, so the operator can make it where a team reads. Dispatched to the notifier, which every install mounts, because the thread is optional and the turn is not.

actions.name: resolve-review-thread
actions.doc: Close one review thread, by its id.

actions.name: run-errand
actions.doc: Do the thing somebody asked for, in their own words.

actions.name: self-review
actions.doc: A workflow-declared half-step: the work reviews itself before a person is asked to.

contracts.doc: The coding agent, and the only probabilistic thing in the system.

methods.name: ask
methods.signature: ask(prompt: string, cwd: string, context?: AskContext): Promise<HarnessReply>

contracts.doc: The narrow source capability grooming receives.
A read-only view of one repository at one commit of its base branch.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: Reads a tracked file as it exists at `revision`.

methods.name: search
methods.doc: Where a text appears at `revision`. Literal by default.

methods.name: history
methods.doc: Commits up to `revision` that added or removed occurrences of a text.

contracts.doc: The mounted persistence port behind every brief read and write.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: The current brief by id, or null when no such brief exists.

methods.name: write
methods.signature: write(input: { id: BriefId; sections: { name: string; body: string }[]; /** The work ids this brief explains, in the caller's own vocabulary. */ explains: string[]; at: string; }): Promise<BriefRecord>
methods.doc: Creates a brief, or replaces every section of an existing one. The id is the caller's to choose and stable for the brief's life; an append is a separate operation, so a revision never loses a question.

methods.name: appendQuestion
methods.signature: appendQuestion(input: { id: BriefId; question: BriefQuestion; at: string }): Promise<BriefRecord>
methods.doc: Appends a question, with its work id and time. There is no operation that appends an answer: a question is decided by the workflow that owns the brief, and that decision is a revision, not an append.

methods.name: retired
methods.signature: retired(explainsAreTerminal: (workId: string) => boolean, retentionCutoffMs: number, now: Date): Promise<BriefId[]>
methods.doc: Lists brief ids whose every work id is terminal and older than the store's retention policy, for the retirement sweep. The caller decides what terminal means in its own vocabulary; this only reports what it was told at write time and cannot invent a work state it never knew.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: Removes a brief by id. The event log remains the durable history.

contracts.doc: Whether work that spends an agent may start.
The forge: a repository, a branch, a pull request and a login.

methods.name: findPullRequest
methods.signature: findPullRequest(repo: string, branch: string): Promise<PullRequestView | null>

methods.name: pullRequestAncestry
methods.signature: pullRequestAncestry(repo: string, number: number): Promise<PullRequestAncestry | null>
methods.doc: The forge facts a stacked child needs to choose its base.

methods.name: findPullRequestMentioning
methods.signature: findPullRequestMentioning(repo: string, id: string): Promise<PullRequestView | null>
methods.doc: The pull request whose title names this id as a whole word, open or merged, in one repository.

methods.name: openPullRequest
methods.doc: Throws a `CodeHostRefusal` when the host answers that it will not; any other throw is a failure.

methods.name: requestReview
methods.signature: requestReview(repo: string, pullRequestNumber: number, host: string): Promise<void>

methods.name: resolveReviewThread
methods.doc: Closes one review thread, by its own id, in one act.

methods.name: unresolveReviewThread
methods.doc: Puts a closed thread back, for a fix that was reverted.

methods.name: reviewLoad
methods.doc: Open reviews per login, counted across every given repository.

methods.name: reviewsRequestedOf
methods.signature: reviewsRequestedOf(login: string, repos: readonly string[]): Promise<ReviewRequest[]>
methods.doc: The open pull requests waiting on one login's review, in these repositories and no others.

methods.name: changesRequestedOf
methods.signature: changesRequestedOf(login: string, repos: readonly string[]): Promise<ReviewRequest[]>
methods.doc: The open pull requests one login's review left changes requested on, in these repositories and no others.

methods.name: authoredWithChangesRequested
methods.signature: authoredWithChangesRequested(login: string, repos: readonly string[]): Promise<ReviewRequest[]>
methods.doc: The open pull requests one login authored that somebody asked to change, in these repositories and no others.

methods.name: pullRequest
methods.signature: pullRequest(repo: string, number: number): Promise<PullRequestView | null>
methods.doc: One pull request by its number, merged or not.

methods.name: merge
methods.signature: merge(repo: string, number: number, method: "merge" | "squash" | "rebase"): Promise<void>
methods.doc: Merges it, by the method the caller named.

methods.name: submitReview
methods.signature: submitReview(repo: string, number: number, review: { state: ReviewState; body: string }): Promise<void>
methods.doc: Submits a review of it, in the state the caller decided on.

methods.name: createIssue
methods.signature: createIssue(repo: string, issue: { title: string; body: string }): Promise<number>
methods.doc: Files an issue in the repository, as the forge writes one.

methods.name: commitStatuses
methods.signature: commitStatuses(repo: string, sha: string): Promise< { context: string; state: "passing" | "failing" | "running" }[] >
methods.doc: The statuses the forge recorded on one commit, as a list.

contracts.doc: Running a child process, behind a port.

methods.name: run
methods.signature: run(command: string, args: readonly string[], options?: RunOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

methods.name: spawn
methods.signature: spawn(command: string, args: readonly string[], options?: Pick<RunOptions, "cwd" | "env">): ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams
methods.doc: So protocol children stop through the same handbrake as ordinary commands.

contracts.doc: Any command line tool, reached by a name somebody put in the config.

methods.name: run
methods.signature: run(name: string, args?: readonly string[], options?: { cwd?: string }): Promise<CommandOutcome>

methods.name: available
methods.doc: What the config allows, for a refusal that names the alternatives.

contracts.doc: Where an operator and one piece of work talk without using the tracker.

methods.name: chat
methods.doc: The messages that reached no work, filed and not yet settled, oldest first. Present only on adapters that answer in the chat; the daemon reads it all the time, and one arriving mid-turn waits for the next turn.

methods.name: settle
methods.doc: The message is answered: it is not handed out again.

methods.name: say
methods.doc: Says something in a chat place, and answers the message's id.

methods.name: revise
methods.signature: revise(place: string, id: string, text: string): Promise<void>

skills.name: amy
skills.description: Drive amy, the machine that walks a work ticket from the tracker's working status to a QA handoff, and turns friction it hits into a plan in the repository that friction is about.

skills.name: amy-btw
skills.description: Capture something said in passing as work amy will actually do — "btw the deps in the api are stale", "also check whether that monitor is still firing" — without opening a ticket and without leaving what you are doing.

skills.name: amy-groom
skills.description: Groom a feature into the brief a workflow reads before it builds — by reading the ticket and the code at its base, then asking one question at a time, section by section in the order the workflow declares them, until `amy brief check` is green.

skills.name: amy-init
skills.description: Set amy up on this machine end to end — the state directory, the config, the roster, the plugins it needs installed, the credentials, the notification channel — by reading what is already here and asking only what the machine cannot answer.

skills.name: amy-show-me
skills.description: Show what an amy workflow is and where its work has got to, visually — the state machine, the path one piece of work took, what is waiting on what.

skills.name: amy-status
skills.description: Answer "where is my work" from the project's side rather than the machine's — what is open, what amy is working on right now, what is waiting on you, what is stuck — across every workflow at once, as a page you can keep open.

skills.name: amy-workflow
skills.description: Design a new amy workflow, or change one that exists, by being interrogated one question at a time until the shape is settled — then write it as its own package.

settings.description: the channel id every work thread opens in, such as C0XXXXXXX — an id, not a name

settings.name: decisionReaction
settings.description: the reaction, by emoji name, the operator puts on their own reply to mark it as the decision that moves the work. A reaction Slack lists only in part is read again in full with reactions.get, which needs reactions:read

settings.name: defaultRetryAfterSeconds
settings.description: how long to wait after a 429 that carries no Retry-After; one names its own wait, and that wins

settings.name: directory
settings.description: where each work item's thread is remembered, relative to the state directory

settings.name: discussionReaction
settings.description: the reaction, by emoji name, the operator puts on their own reply to mark it as a turn in a discussion, answered in the thread while the work waits

settings.name: maxRateLimitRetries
settings.description: how many times a call Slack rate limits (HTTP 429) is waited out and tried again before it fails

settings.name: operator
settings.description: the user id, such as U0XXXXXXX, whose replies are answers; everybody else's are ignored

settings.name: retentionDays
settings.description: days a downloaded file or a thread's memory stays unused before it is pruned, 0 to keep everything. A pruned file is fetched again when its reply is read; a pruned thread means the next question opens a new one

settings.name: token
settings.description: where the bot token lives: `env:SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` or `file:<path>#<KEY>`, never the token itself

shipped.name: @amykit/plugin-telegram
shipped.description: A topic per piece of work in the operator's private chat with a Telegram bot, as the conversation port.

settings.name: directory
settings.description: where this profile's topics are remembered, by work id, relative to the state directory; the replies read for every profile are kept once per bot

settings.name: operator
settings.description: your Telegram user id, a number such as 123456789: the private chat each work item's topic opens in, and the only person whose replies are answers

settings.name: server
settings.description: the Bot API server, for a local one instead of Telegram's

settings.name: topics
settings.description: whether each piece of work opens a topic of its own; off, works share the private chat and a reply reaches one by quoting amy's message for it or starting with its id

shipped.name: @amykit/plugin-terminal
shipped.description: Drives an interactive terminal program through terminal-use: run it, type, press keys, wait for text and read the screen.

settings.name: binary
settings.description: the terminal-use command, or a path to it

settings.name: session
settings.description: the terminal-use session every operation drives, so steps of one scenario share one program

settings.name: timeoutMs
settings.description: how long one terminal-use command may run, past any wait it was asked for

shipped.name: @amykit/plugin-terminal-conversation
shipped.description: The person's terminal as an amy conversation: asks post to stdout, and answers come back as a line or a number.

shipped.name: @amykit/services
shipped.description: amy's own domains: every operation declared once, with its documentation, and the OpenAPI document every door is read from.

shipped.name: @amykit/ui
shipped.description: A view is data: a closed vocabulary of primitives, JSX without React, diff and patch, a text renderer, and the closed frame every renderer is measured against.

shipped.name: @amykit/ui-conformance
shipped.description: The frame's conformance script: drives a renderer by keys, by a remapped keymap and by the mouse, and holds what it laid out to the frame, to the other renderers and to the approved golden.

shipped.name: @amykit/workflow-errand
shipped.description: Something said in passing becomes work: capture it, do it, say what happened.

settings.name: baseBranch
settings.description: where one repository's base branch is, instead of the fallback. A repository named here has its work cut from, and its pull requests opened against, that branch

settings.name: defaultBranch
settings.description: the branch new work is cut from, for a repository that named none, which is not always `main`

settings.name: policy.ceilingBackoffMs
settings.description: how long a task is held while the in-flight ceiling is reached

settings.name: policy.maxAttempts
settings.description: how many times an agent may try one errand before it is handed back

settings.name: policy.maxInFlight
settings.description: how many errands this machine may carry in flight at once. Capturing costs nothing, which is the whole point and also the failure, and past this many it holds rather than opening another pull request nobody asked to review

settings.name: queueDirectory
settings.description: where this machine keeps the queue `amy btw` puts the task on, relative to the state root. The host sets it; a value here only stands in for one

settings.name: repos
settings.description: where an errand may be done. The machine's own list of repositories names this by default, and a profile narrows or widens it. An errand about a place not on the list is handed back to whoever asked

settings.name: tasksDirectory
settings.description: where this machine keeps the tasks `amy btw` writes, relative to the state root. The host sets it; a value here only stands in for one

settings.name: defaultBranch
settings.description: the branch new work is cut from, for a repository that named none, which is not always `main`

settings.name: policy.briefLookMs

settings.name: repos

shipped.name: @amykit/workflow-note-to-plan
shipped.description: The note-to-plan workflow: friction becomes a plan in the repository it is about.

settings.name: baseBranch
settings.description: where one repository's base branch is, instead of the fallback. A repository named here has its work cut from, and its pull requests opened against, that branch

settings.name: check
settings.description: the check commands per repository, with a `default` fallback, that judge a plan before it goes anywhere. `sf check` is the whole quality bar in a repository that has one; the plan-check plugin mounts them

settings.name: defaultBranch
settings.description: the branch new work is cut from, for a repository that named none, which is not always `main`

settings.name: notesDirectory
settings.description: where this machine keeps the notes `amy note` writes, relative to the state root. The host sets it; a value here only stands in for one

settings.name: policy.ceilingBackoffMs
settings.description: how long a note is held while the plan ceiling is reached

settings.name: policy.maxDraftAttempts
settings.description: how many times an agent may try to write a plan the check accepts before it is handed back

settings.name: policy.maxOpenPlansPerRepo
settings.description: how many plans this machine may carry in flight for one repository. A machine that files twelve plans a day into three repositories is producing a backlog with a robot's name on it, and past this many it holds

settings.name: queueDirectory
settings.description: where this machine keeps the queue `amy note` puts the note on, relative to the state root. The host sets it; a value here only stands in for one

settings.name: repos
settings.description: the repositories a plan may be written into. A note about anything else is handed back to the operator

shipped.name: @amykit/workflow-pull-request
shipped.description: A workflow other workflows call: open a pull request for a branch, through whichever code host is mounted.

settings.name: draft
settings.description: open the pull request as a draft, for work nobody is waiting on at the moment it lands

settings.name: policy.settleMs
settings.description: how long to wait for a pull request the host opened to show, before looking again

shipped.name: @amykit/workflow-setup
shipped.description: Onboarding as an amy workflow: amy setup walks a fresh machine through harness, workflow and channels, one ask at a time.

settings.name: policy.askBackoffMs
settings.description: how long the walk waits between looks at an ask the person has not answered

shipped.name: @amykit/workflow-testkit
shipped.description: The tests every workflow needs and nobody writes, driven against a world its author supplies.

shipped.name: @amykit/workflow-ticket-to-qa
shipped.description: The ticket-to-QA workflow: its states, its typed port contracts, and a pure plan().

settings.name: baseBranch
settings.description: where one repository's base branch is, instead of the fallback. A repository named here has its work cut from, and its pull requests opened against, that branch

settings.name: budget
settings.description: agent budget, including an optional progress block that stops repeated no-evidence runs

settings.name: defaultBranch
settings.description: the branch new work is cut from, for a repository that named none, which is not always `main`

settings.name: policy.conversation
settings.description: answer: a reply in the work's thread is your decision, and the work moves on it. discuss: a reply is a turn in a discussion, answered in the thread while the work waits; mark the reply that decides and only that one moves it. A reply you marked reads as marked under either, and without a thread a comment on the ticket is always the decision

settings.name: policy.maxGateAttempts
settings.description: how many times the gate may see one change before the work is escalated

settings.name: policy.maxImplementAttempts
settings.description: how many times an agent may try to implement one ticket before it is escalated

settings.name: policy.maxOpenReviewsPerReviewer
settings.description: how many open reviews one person may be carrying before this machine stops adding to their pile. Review time is somebody else's, and it is the one currency here that cannot be topped up

settings.name: policy.maxPullRequestFiles
settings.description: how large a pull request may get, in files, before this machine stops handing it to an agent. The forge has already told us the size, so a pull request nobody should automate is handed back before an agent is called. Zero switches it off

settings.name: policy.maxPullRequestLines
settings.description: how large a pull request may get, in changed lines, under the same rule as maxPullRequestFiles. Zero switches it off

settings.name: policy.pollBackoffMs
settings.description: how long a waiting state holds before it looks again: waiting on an answer, or on a review

settings.name: policy.rosterBackoffMs
settings.description: how long to hold while the roster is waiting to be confirmed

settings.name: policy.writes
settings.description: machine: amy comments, opens pull requests, requests reviews and moves the ticket to QA. operator: each of those is said to you once instead, and amy waits until it sees you made it. Nothing is written on the tracker or the code host

settings.name: qaStatusName
settings.description: the status a ticket moves to when it is handed to QA

settings.name: repos
settings.description: every repository review load is counted across

settings.name: reviewerHints
settings.description: guidance appended to the review prompt when answering a particular reviewer, by host login
